traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Potamogetonaceae with Ruppiaceae, Zannichelliaceae, which APG and WCVP join to it (their extra states read as sometimes): leaves usually alternate, sometimes opposite, rarely whorled; leaves simple; margins usually entire, sometimes serrate; veins single, palmate or parallel; blades linear, oblong or ovate; stipules usually absent, rarely present; leaf rosettes none; plants usually hermaphrodite, sometimes monoecious or dioecious; ovary superior; stems herbaceous; flowers usually in racemes, sometimes solitary, in spikes, in umbels or in cymes; flowers actinomorphic; perianth usually tepals, sometimes absent; fruit nut, aggregate or achene, sometimes follicle; parts of each whorl 4; stamens 4; carpels (3-) 4 (-8). Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: DELTA Potamogetonaceae (read 2026-10-16): leaves mostly alternate and then two-ranked.

traits.leaf_shape.note: FNA Potamogeton (read 2026-10-17): ~100 spp, the bulk of the family; submersed blades range from linear to nearly round, floating ones elliptic to ovate. Wikipedia Potamogeton (read 2026-10-17) splits the genus into a linear-leaved and a broad-leaved group. The joined genera Stuckenia, Zannichellia, Ruppia and Groenlandia are all narrow-leaved, which tips the lead to linear; broad shapes stay common, hence often.
